trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 3 rows of primitives (c,d), their S-images and det T. RECOMPUTED: the three rows are mutually consistent with, and jointly determine, det T(1,d) = d^2 + h_A d - 1 -- d=0 gives -1 (row uu), d=-h_A gives -1 (row dd), d=-h_A/2 gives -(h_A^2/4+1) (row ud); all three printed dets match. INDEPENDENT INVARIANT: the tabulated S acts as d -> -h_A - d, which is an involution (S(1,0)=(1,-h_A), S(1,-h_A)=(1,0), S(1,-h_A/2) fixed -- all as printed) and leaves d^2+h_A d invariant, so det T(S(c,d)) = det T(c,d) identically. That is why the fourth and fifth columns agree in every row, and it is a genuine derivation rather than a coincidence of the three sampled points. No numerics, no q_0, no braid words.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: Clean. Note only that the ud row's fixed point d=-h_A/2 is the unique S-fixed primitive, which is the structural reason chirality (the S-odd direction) cannot be seen from it -- consistent with the parent's conclusion.
